claims.name: Raspberry Pi Pico (device)
claims.statement: Physical microcontroller running the CircuitPython firmware, connected to the DJ's PC over USB.

claims.name: DJ's PC (Mixxx host)
claims.statement: Windows PC running Mixxx DJ Software, which loads the DJMixer.js controller script from the user's local app-data folder.

attrs.technology: Windows (implied by %LOCALAPPDATA% path); Mixxx DJ Software

claims.name: GPIO pin assignments
claims.statement: Physical GPIO pins are hardcoded in main.py to specific control functions (A0=volume, A1=crossfader, GP14/GP15=cue buttons, GP0-2=LEDs).

attrs.where_set: main.py source, wired to match Readme's wiring diagram
attrs.influences: Which physical pin drives which control

claims.name: MIDI channel / CC / note numbers
claims.statement: MIDI channel (1) and CC/note numbers (7, 8, 20, 21) are hardcoded constants matching the Mixxx MIDI mapping XML.

attrs.where_set: main.py constructor calls, mirrored in DJMixer.midi.xml
attrs.influences: Which Mixxx control a given physical input drives

claims.name: potentiometerSensitivity
claims.statement: Threshold below which a knob movement is treated as jitter and ignored, hardcoded to 2 (out of a 0-127 MIDI range).

claims.name: PuTTY serial connection
claims.statement: Manual REPL testing connects over a COM port at 115200 baud.

attrs.where_set: chosen per-machine in PuTTY, not in source
attrs.influences: Ability to interactively test the device

claims.name: No automated deployment
claims.statement: Firmware install is a fully manual drag-and-drop of three files onto a USB mass-storage drive; the Mixxx script install is a manual copy into a fixed folder. No script or CI automates either.

claims.name: No health/liveness signal
claims.statement: Nothing in the firmware or the Mixxx script reports its own health; a hung polling loop or a disconnected device is only noticeable by the DJ losing control mid-set.
